scope: Static review of main exception handling, descriptor custody, deadline and publication success gate only
observations: One exact stopped synthetic root and process.log are addressed; all ancestors are walked through held dirfds with O_NOFOLLOW and named identity checks before and after the read.
The leaf is regular, UID 1000, mode 0600, nlink 1, and bounded at 2 MiB. Complete bytes, one-byte EOF and unchanged held/named full file metadata are required before observed/complete are set.

The deferred signal flag avoids a Python exception between open and descriptor registration. Every registered descriptor is visited once in the final reverse close loop; an OSError makes complete false and prevents a successful exit.

Remaining-time guards span path walking, each read, each parsed line, final held/named checks, closure and publication. The post-flush remaining(until) guard prevents exit 0 after the original 15-second observation deadline.
Only the two exact marker grammars, the closed step/code sets and bounded numeric/hash fields are emitted. Other lines are counted but their contents are not emitted.
An empty marker set does not claim absence of an internal failure. The source explicitly disclaims cross-request correlation.
caller_requirements: The source_sha256_argument is syntactically checked, not an in-process proof of source bytes; the external exact-source/argv admission remains necessary.
Stopped-fixture ownership is established by the previously accepted terminal/cleanup evidence. This read-only filter does not re-probe processes.

Use authoritative exit 0 with the complete output and closed descriptors. The publication_within_original_deadline flag alone is set before write/flush and is not a replacement for the post-flush exit gate.
